01
Stage 01 · Eligibility

Capability Questionnaire

Before the assessment starts, we need the basics: what you make, how big you are, your accreditations, your financial standing, your safety and quality track record. It's background information, not a test — most companies get through it in well under an hour.

Pass this and a Supply Chain Consultant is assigned to you as your named point of contact for the rest of the journey. This isn't a portal you're left alone with.

Typical time
< 1 hour
Outcome
Eligibility + your SCC

02
Stage 02 · Self-diagnosis

Business Excellence self-assessment

This is where it gets real. 60 questions across six areas — Strategy & Leadership, Design & Project Management, People Excellence, Process Excellence, QHSE, and Supply Chain & Social Values. Business Excellence is the spine of the whole assessment: everything nuclear-specific later builds on top of it.

For each question, you pick one of four options that best describes where your company actually is today — and anything beyond the most basic answer needs evidence to back it up at verification. Below are four real questions from the actual question bank, so you can see the level of scrutiny involved. Try selecting your position on each.

Why it matters beyond nuclear: these six areas aren't sector box-ticking — they're what separates a well-run manufacturer from an average one, full stop. A clear strategy people actually know, a workforce that's engaged and developing, processes that don't rely on tribal knowledge, disciplined QHSE, a supply chain that collaborates rather than just transacts — get good at these and the business runs better regardless of who you sell to. Nuclear-readiness is the by-product, not the whole point.

These four options are illustrative of what verification actually checks for — where you land honestly is the point. The Members Area handbooks exist to help you move up, and your SCC is with you the whole way.
03
Stage 03 · Verification

On-Site Verification (OSV)

A full-day site visit where your SCC checks your self-assessment against real evidence — documents, a shop-floor walk, conversations with your team. It isn't pass/fail. It's diagnostic: the point is to find out exactly where the gaps are, so the next stage has something to aim at.

You get a written report afterwards with verified scores against every category, alongside your own self-assessed figures — the two columns rarely match on the first pass, and that's expected.

  • Facility tour and document review, category by category
  • Time with leadership and with shop-floor staff
  • A written report: verified scores, evidence gaps, suggested improvements
f4n.nuccol.co.uk/progress

Self-assessed vs. SCC-verified, side by side, category by category — the gap between the two columns is where Stage 4 begins.

04
Stage 04 · Close the gaps

Action Plan

Not left to work it out alone

A page of red scores and overdue flags can look daunting on its own. This is where it stops being a list of what's wrong and starts being a plan for what's next: every gap becomes a SMART action — specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound — with an owner and a deadline.

And for every action, there's a way in: your SCC to talk it through, a handbook topic with step-by-step guidance on that exact question, a short knowledge video if you just need the two-minute version, and a toolbox template so you're implementing, not starting from a blank page.

Nothing gets submitted into a void. Every action you mark complete is reviewed by your SCC, with feedback given, and tracked in the portal against your target score — so you always know whether "done" actually means done.

Handbook

Step-by-step guidance written against this exact question, not generic advice.

Knowledge video

A short, plain-English explainer to get the whole team up to speed fast.

Toolbox

A ready-made template to implement the fix, not just describe it.

05
Stage 05 · Sector-specific

Nuclear Sector Specific (NSS) assessment

The nuclear-specific half of the assessment is introduced later on purpose — usually 3–4 months before your expected Granting date, once your Business Excellence score is closing in on the required standard. Bring it in too early and it overwhelms companies who are still finding their feet on the fundamentals.

It covers things a generic quality system doesn't touch: nuclear safety culture, human performance, ISO 19443, supply-chain traceability, CFSI. See if your team could answer these with confidence — and with evidence.

Same rigor, same procedure. NSS isn't graded any differently to Business Excellence — it follows the same three steps: self-assessment, on-site verification, action plan. Nothing about the process gets softer just because the content gets more technical.

06
Stage 06 · Prove it

Pre-Granting preparation

An in-depth review, led by your SCC, to confirm the improvements are real — not just marked complete on the portal. Every action needs its evidence attached: a policy, a photo, a certificate, a record.

85³

The "Triple 85"

NucCol's shorthand for the eligibility bar a company has to clear across the programme before it can go in front of the Granting Panel. Your SCC will tell you exactly where you stand against it.

f4n.nuccol.co.uk/action-plan

07
Stage 07 · The panel

NucCol Granting Panel

A formal panel of senior NucCol programme leaders — sometimes with sector specialists in the room — reviews the entire journey and decides whether to award Fit For Nuclear status. Your SCC has already told you if you're ready; this is where it's confirmed.

What actually goes in front of them:

  • A Business Excellence summary with verified scores across all 60 questions
  • Commentary on strengths and gaps addressed, category by category
  • A completed Action Plan with evidence attached
  • A completed Nuclear Sector Specific assessment
  • Supporting documentation — certificates, policies, H&S records, photographs
  • A signed F4N Charter and Benefits Statement
f4n.nuccol.co.uk/recommendation

Your SCC's own recommendation to the panel — built from everything on file, not a fresh opinion on the day.

08
Stage 08 · Post-granting

Maintain & Sustain (M&S)

Granted isn't the finish line — it's what moves you into Maintain & Sustain, NucCol's ongoing membership for companies who've made it through. You're listed on the NucCol website and on NuclearReady, visible to the buyers and tier-1s actually searching against it, and you can put together your own F4N case study to show off how you got there.

You keep full access to everything in your Members Area — both handbooks, the toolbox, the videos, webinars. There's no reassessment to sit through: it's an annual subscription, with two visits a year from your SCC to keep things on track, plus monthly sector updates and the live tenders feed landing in your account the whole time.
